elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in any Calendar Year". Calendar Year is defined as the Jan 1–Dec 31 period, so two audits could still fall in December and the following January, i.e. within a single rolling 12-month period. A "once in any twelve (12)-month period" formulation would be needed for the preferred element.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a) sets notice at "at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" — the fallback figure, not the 30 days required at the preferred level.

elements.element: Audits occur during business hours.
elements.evidence: No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in 9.9(a)-(d); the drafter expressly declines to press this point.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) (unchanged): "permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: 9.9(d) (unchanged): the Parties "shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence"; 9.9(b) also bars disclosure of the audited Party's Confidential Information beyond verification needs.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site/remote-review preference is stated in 9.9; the clause is silent on audit location.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c) shifts cost only where the underpayment "was more than ten percent (10%)" — the fallback threshold, above the 5% preferred trigger.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) confines the auditor to "the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8" and 9.9(b) limits the report, but there is no express prohibition on access to Customer systems and no statement that records are produced rather than accessed in situ; scope limitation implies but does not operatively state the no-system-access element.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in any Calendar Year", with the open-ended "unless for cause" carve-out deleted, so the annual cap is a hard ceiling with a definite number replacing the [***] placeholder.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "but in any event at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" replaces the [***] placeholder with an operative 15-day floor.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c): "The auditing Party shall bear the full cost of such audit unless such audit reveals an underpayment ... more than ten percent (10%) of the amount set forth in such report" — cost sits with the auditing (Vendor) side unless the 10% trigger is exceeded.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative face of the rendered clause: a hard once-per-Calendar-Year cap, a 15-day prior notice floor, and Vendor-side cost bearing unless underpayment exceeds 10%. Each replaced a redacted [***] placeholder that left the limit unenforceable, so the original clause did fail the fallback on material terms and the 'deviation' classification is correct.

Deletion of the "unless for cause" carve-out is necessary rather than cosmetic: without it the annual cap is not a ceiling at all, so it is properly within the frequency element and does not break minimality.

Minimality otherwise holds — no survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra requirements were added, and the favourable existing terms (independent auditor of international prominence, auditor confidentiality agreement, report-scope limits, books-and-records-only scope, interest and dispute mechanics) are untouched. The single added word "written" in the notice sentence is a de minimis modifier that tracks the rule's own notice element; it is noted but not treated as a minimality failure.

Intent is preserved: the clause remains mutual as originally drafted (Section 6.9 running the other way is left alone), no cross-reference is orphaned, and the remaining [***] placeholders (record look-back period in 9.9(a) and payment window in 9.9(b)) are pre-existing redactions the edit did not create or contradict.

Preferred level is not reached and the rationale correctly does not claim it. If the drafter wants to push to preferred, the operative repairs are: change "once in any Calendar Year" to "once in any twelve (12)-month period" (a Calendar Year cap permits back-to-back December/January audits), raise notice to "thirty (30) days", lower the cost-shift trigger in 9.9(c) to "five percent (5%)", add "during the audited Party's normal business hours" and an "off-site where reasonably possible" preference, and add an express statement that the auditor shall have no direct access to the audited Party's systems or networks.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

paragraphs.text: REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS; CLOSING CONDITIONS
13.1 Representations and Warranties of Each Party. Each Party hereby represents and warrants, as of the Execution, and covenants (as applicable) to the other Party as follows:

(a) It is a company or corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction in which it is incorporated, and has the full right, power and authority to enter into this Agreement, to perform its obligations hereunder.

(b) (i) This Agreement has been duly executed by it and is legally binding upon it, enforceable in accordance with its terms, (ii) it has taken all necessary corporate action on its part required to authorize the execution and delivery of this Agreement and, (iii) this Agreement, and the performance of its obligations hereunder, do not conflict with any agreement, instrument or understanding, oral or written, to which it is a party or by which it may be bound, nor violate any material law or regulation of any court, governmental body or administrative or other agency having jurisdiction over it.

(c) (i) It is familiar with the provisions and restrictions contained in the FCPA and has adopted and maintains an FCPA policy; (ii) it shall comply with the FCPA in connection with its activities under this Agreement; (iii) it shall not, in the course of its activities under this Agreement, offer, promise, give, demand, seek or accept, directly or indirectly, any gift or payment, consideration or benefit in kind that would or could be construed as an illegal or corrupt practice; and (iv) it is not a government official (as the term is defined in the FCPA) or affiliated with any government official.

(d) (i) Neither it nor any of its Affiliates has been debarred or is subject to debarment pursuant to Section 306 of the FFDCA or analogous provisions of Applicable Law outside the United States or listed on any Excluded List and (ii) neither it nor any of its Affiliates has, to its knowledge, used in any capacity, in connection with the activities to be performed under this Agreement, any individual or entity that has been debarred pursuant to Section 306 of the FFDCA or analogous provisions of Applicable Law outside the United States, or that is the subject of a conviction described in such Section or analogous provisions of Applicable Law outside the United States, or listed on any Excluded List.

(e) It will maintain throughout the Term all permits, licenses, registrations and other forms of authorizations and approvals from any Governmental Authority, necessary or required to be obtained or maintained by such Party in order for such Party to execute and deliver this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder in a manner which complies with all Applicable Law. 66

13.2 Representations and Warranties by RevMed. Except as disclosed in the Disclosure Schedule to this Agreement in Exhibit N of the Correspondence, RevMed represents and warrants to Sanofi as of the Execution Date that:
(a) RevMed has not had any Affiliates prior to the Execution Date and does not have any Affiliates as of the Execution Date;

(b) RevMed is the sole and exclusive owner of all of the RevMed Background Technology, free and clear or all liens and encumbrances, and no Third Party owns or possesses any right, title or interest in or to any of the RevMed Licensed Technology existing as of the Execution Date;

(c) RevMed has not previously agreed to or otherwise committed to assign, transfer or convey or otherwise encumber its rights, title and interests in and to RevMed Licensed Technology existing as of the Execution Date;

(d) To the Knowledge of RevMed, all Patent Rights owned or Controlled by RevMed, existing as of the Execution Date, and reasonably necessary or useful for conducting the Collaboration or otherwise necessary or useful for Researching, Developing, Manufacturing, Commercializing or otherwise exploiting Product in the Field, including the Development or Manufacture of the Products as contemplated in the initial Research Plan and Development Plan attached to this Agreement as of the Execution Date and Commercialization of the Products, as provided hereunder are listed in Exhibit O of the Correspondence;

(e) RevMed has the right to grant the licenses and other rights expressly granted herein to Sanofi, and it has not granted any license, right or interest in, to or under the RevMed Licensed Technology to any Third Party (or agreed to make any such grant) to exploit SHP2 Inhibitors or Products in the Field;

(f) To RevMed's Knowledge, the research and development of the Development Candidate and use of RevMed Background Know-How in connection therewith does not infringe the claims of any issued Patent or published patent application of any Third Party;
(g) The research and development of the SHP2 Inhibitors and use of RevMed Background Know-How in connection therewith does not misappropriate the Know-How of any Third Party;

(h) The research and development of SHP2 Inhibitors (including pursuant to the activities set forth in the initial Research Plan and initial Development Plan) does not breach any obligation of confidentiality or non-use owed by RevMed to a Third Party;
(i) To RevMed's Knowledge, no Third Parties are misappropriating the RevMed Background Know-How and there are no activities by Third Parties that are infringing the RevMed Background Patents; 67

(j) There are no judgments or settlements against or owed by RevMed, and to RevMed's Knowledge, there are no pending claims or litigation or written threats of possible claims or litigation, in each case relating to the SHP2 Inhibitors or otherwise to RevMed Background Technology;

(k) The issued RevMed Background Patents are valid, enforceable and subsisting, and the pending applications included in the RevMed Background Patents are being prosecuted in accordance with Applicable Law in all material respects, and RevMed has presented all relevant references, documents and information of which it and the inventors are aware to the relevant patent examiners and patent offices that are required to be so submitted under Applicable Law;
(l) The RevMed Background Patents have been filed and maintained properly and correctly and all applicable fees have been paid on or before the due date for payment in all material respects;

(m) RevMed has not received any written notice alleging that the RevMed Background Patents, existing as of the Execution Date, are or would be invalid or unenforceable or that the applications included in such RevMed Background Patents will not proceed to grant;

(n) There (i) are no actual, pending or, to RevMed's Knowledge, alleged or threatened, adverse actions, suits, claims, interferences, re-examinations, oppositions, inventorship challenges or formal governmental investigations involving the RevMed Background Technology that are in or before any Governmental Authority, and (ii) are no actual, pending or, to RevMed's Knowledge, alleged or threatened, adverse actions, suits, claims, interferences, re-examinations, oppositions, inventorship challenges or formal governmental investigations involving the RevMed Licensed Technology;

(o) The inventions claimed or covered by the RevMed Licensed Technology (i) were not conceived, discovered, developed or otherwise made in connection with any research activities funded, in whole or in part, by the federal government of the United States or any agency thereof, (ii) are not a "subject invention" as that term is described in 35 U.S.C. § 201(e), (iii) are not otherwise subject to the provisions of the Patent and Trademark Law Amendments Act of 1980, as amended, codified at 35 U.S.C. §§ 200-212, as amended, as well as any regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, including in 37 C.F.R. part 401, and (iv) are not the subject of any licenses, options or other rights of any other Governmental Authority, within or outside the United States, due to such Governmental Authority's funding of research and development or otherwise (other than the right to receive payments or any law of general application that applies to personal property generally, e.g., takings laws);
(p) None of the RevMed Background Patents are licensed to RevMed from a Third Party;

(q) There are no exclusivity provisions or any other restrictions in any agreement between RevMed or its Affiliates, on the one hand, and any Third Party, on the other hand, of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product, that would limit Sanofi's ability to exercise its rights under this Agreement; 68

(r) All current and former officers, employees, and consultants of RevMed who are inventors of or have otherwise contributed in a material manner to the creation or development of any RevMed Background Technology have executed and delivered to RevMed an assignment or other agreement regarding the protection of proprietary information and the assignment to RevMed of inventions or work product created or generated in the course of employment by or providing services for RevMed, the current forms of which has been made available for review by Sanofi;

(s) The portions of RevMed Background Know-How that are proprietary to RevMed and unpublished as of the Execution Date and material to Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of SHP2 Inhibitors or Products in the Field have been kept confidential by RevMed and have only been disclosed to Third Parties under obligations of confidentiality, and to the Knowledge of RevMed, no such Third Party has breached any such confidentiality obligation to RevMed;

(t) RevMed has included in the electronic dataroom for this Agreement all information in its possession that is material to the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of the Development Candidate as of the Execution Date, and such information does not contain any untrue statement(s) of fact, or omit to state any fact(s), in either case that are collectively material to the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of the Development Candidate; and
(u) To RevMed's Knowledge, RevMed and its contractors and consultants have conducted all research and development of the SHP2 Inhibitors and Products in material compliance with all Applicable Laws.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",

elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained in 15.2(a)(i): "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi". Sanofi is Customer; the no-consent affiliate right is preserved unaltered by the redline.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rewritten 15.2(a)(ii) first prong: "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser ... in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction." All three trigger events (merger, acquisition, substantially-all-assets sale) survive the split.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Chapeau 15.2(a) bars assignment "without the consent of the other Party, except as follows", and both retained exceptions for RevMed are now consent-gated: affiliate assignment "with the consent of Sanofi" (i) and Change of Control successor assignment "with the consent of Sanofi" (ii). No residual no-consent path for RevMed remains.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: 15.2(a)(i) retains "(not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned)" and the new 15.2(a)(ii) RevMed prong adds "(not to be unreasonably withheld)". Every operative RevMed assignment permission carries the reasonableness standard; the chapeau's bare consent for unenumerated assignments is pre-existing and outside the element.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "In no event shall RevMed assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder to a competitor of Sanofi." Unconditional and covers rights/obligations as well as the whole Agreement, so the Change of Control acquirer route cannot be used to reach a Sanofi competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3(c) enumerates RevMed's termination grounds exhaustively as 12.2(b) material breach, 12.2(c) insolvency, 12.2(d) Sanofi Competing Product and 12.2(e) cessation — none keyed to a Sanofi Change of Control; the only CoC-based termination is Sanofi's own right under 12.2(a)(ii)A, which runs in our favour and is untouched.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the redline only Sanofi may assign to a successor "without consent of RevMed"; RevMed's successor/Change of Control assignment is permitted only "with the consent of Sanofi". That is a consent-gated permission, not the mutual successor right the fallback requires.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Neither prong of 15.2(a)(ii) nor the chapeau imposes any notice obligation; no written-notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Other assignments require consent.
elements.evidence: Sanofi's retained no-consent affiliate exception in 15.2(a)(i) is a non-successor assignment permitted without consent, which defeats this element under the ASSIGN fallback rule.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The chapeau consent requirement for assignments outside the enumerated exceptions carries no reasonableness qualifier; the "not to be unreasonably withheld" language appears only in the two RevMed-specific exceptions.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the two Customer-side carve-outs are retained verbatim, RevMed's previously unconditional Change of Control assignment is now consent-gated with a reasonableness standard, an express competitor bar is added, and no Vendor termination right attaches to a Sanofi Change of Control.

The fallback is deliberately not reached (successor assignment is not mutual and unconditional, no written-notice mechanic, and Sanofi's no-consent affiliate exception defeats "other assignments require consent"), which is acceptable because completion at the preferred level suffices and the fallback would surrender Sanofi's no-consent affiliate right.

Minimal: the only structural change is splitting the former "Either Party may, without consent" sentence into party-specific prongs so the consent gate can attach to RevMed alone; Sanofi's prong, the affiliate prong and the chapeau are unchanged, and the single added sentence is required by the competitor-bar element. No survival tails, notice procedures, expense language or other extras were introduced.

Preserves intent: the Change of Control definition, Sanofi's 12.2(a)(ii)A termination right and the Section 12.3(c) effect-of-termination cross-references remain operative and uncontradicted; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): consider confirming that no other provision (e.g. Competing Product/acquiror mechanics keyed to a RevMed Change of Control) presupposes an unconsented RevMed assignment to its acquirer, so the new consent gate cannot be read as inconsistent with those provisions.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ('Sanofi Indemnitees')" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 lead-in covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees (Sanofi and its Affiliates); "Third Party Claims" is a defined term (1.126).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any Third Party Claim alleging that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party." There are no "Services" or "Deliverables" in this collaboration/licence structure; "RevMed Licensed Technology" (defined at 1.99) plus exercise of the granted licences is the correct analogue, so the element is met in substance. The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" keys on the absent Services/Deliverables vocabulary (and reflects the pre-redline baseline); inspected substantively, the operative limb supplies the IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law" — a free-standing limb that does not depend on the double-materiality filter in retained limb (c)/Section 13.4(b); "Applicable Law" is defined at 1.8.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data caused by RevMed" — causation by Vendor is express.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained limb (a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — ordinary negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is named.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(a): "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses ..." and the notice applies to claims "under Section 14.1 or Section 14.2", so it picks up the new limbs automatically.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ... may select and appoint the lead legal counsel."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(e) Cooperation: "the Indemnified Party will, and will cause each other Indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 as rendered contains only "(a) any content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with former limbs (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]" and the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization and Sanofi-negligence limbs removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.1(d) covers Third Party Claims that the RevMed Licensed Technology or Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences infringes or misappropriates Third Party IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification carve-out is included, which is Customer-favourable and therefore does not defeat the element ("may exclude").

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out is included; the absence of a permitted exclusion is favourable to Customer and does not fail the checklist.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specification carve-out is included; again favourable to Customer, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered Article XIV (or Article XIII) obliges RevMed to procure continued rights, modify or replace infringing technology; Section 10.7 only requires the Parties to negotiate a Third Party licence.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees remedy appears anywhere in the rendered language; there is no fall-back monetary remedy tied to failure of the (absent) procure/modify/replace ladder.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fees super-cap is inserted; the drafter expressly declined it, and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met in operative language. Limbs (d)-(f) supply the missing IP-infringement, data-breach and breach-of-Applicable-Law heads; limbs (a) and the Section 14.3 machinery were already compliant and were correctly left untouched.

The deterministic flag "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" is a vocabulary artefact (the agreement has no "Services"/"Deliverables"); inspected in substance, new Section 14.1(d) is a genuine, unqualified IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity keyed to the defined term "RevMed Licensed Technology" (Section 1.99) and to Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund remedy, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete; the drafter's reasons for declining the super-cap (it would cap a presently uncapped indemnity under Section 14.5) are sound and consistent with not flagging Customer-favourable terms.

Minimal: the edits are confined to the checklist. The conforming change of the exception lead-in from "(a) through (c)" to "(a) through (f)" is necessary to avoid a dangling cross-reference; the deletions in Section 14.2 are required by the tenth preferred element; no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added. Limb (e)'s reference to "Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data" is an acceptable proxy for an undefined "Customer Data" and covers all data belonging to or supplied by Customer rather than selected categories.

Preserves intent: the Section 14.1 carve-outs (i)-(iii) for Sanofi negligence and Sanofi breach survive without contradiction and now properly reach the new limbs; Section 14.3's notice/control/cooperation machinery references "Section 14.1 or Section 14.2" generically and needs no amendment; no defined term is left undefined and the "[Intentionally omitted.]" placeholders preserve internal lettering.

Drafting nit (not a failure): limb (d) reads "arising or resulting from ... any Third Party Claim alleging that ..." against a lead-in that already covers "Third Party Claims". Consider trimming (d) to "an allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party" to remove the circularity.

Practical check before sending: confirm that no other provision (e.g., insurance, the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, or product-liability cost-sharing) cross-refers to the deleted Section 14.2(a)-(d) limbs, since removing Sanofi's Commercialization and negligence indemnities is a substantial reallocation that RevMed will resist; the narrowing is checklist-required, but a residual product-liability cost-share reference would need conforming.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.",
  "Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.",
  "The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.",
  "The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.",
  "The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.",
  "Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.",
  "Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.",
  "Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.",
  "Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees."
]

input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: Section 14.1 gives us a defend-and-indemnify obligation from RevMed covering its negligence, recklessness and willful misconduct and its breaches of warranties and obligations (which, read with the Section 13.4(b) compliance covenant, captures RevMed's breach of Applicable Law), and Section 14.3 supplies the standard notice, control-of-defence and cooperation procedure. However, no limb reaches Third Party claims that the licensed technology or our exercise of the licences infringes or misappropriates Third Party intellectual property, and Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty; Section 10.7 only obliges us to negotiate Third Party licences. That is the walk-away case of no Vendor IP indemnity, so the clause fails even the fallback. We target the preferred position: we add an IP infringement/misappropriation limb and an unauthorised-access/disclosure limb to Section 14.1 (with a conforming cross-reference fix) and narrow our reciprocal Section 14.2 indemnity to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law. We do not take the fallback because its 3x annual-fees super-cap would cut back an indemnity that is presently uncapped (Section 14.5 preserves indemnity claims) and "annual fees" has no counterpart in this milestone/royalty structure.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of the review (INDEMN — deviation, preferred target):**

- **What exists:** Section 14.1 already gives us a RevMed defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Sanofi and its Affiliates against Third Party Claims arising from RevMed's negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct and its breaches of warranties/obligations (which, with the Section 13.4(b) compliance covenant, captures breach of Applicable Law). Section 14.3 supplies notice, control of defence and cooperation.
- **The gap:** no limb reaches Third Party IP infringement/misappropriation, and Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty; Section 10.7 only requires the parties to negotiate a Third Party licence (and gives Sanofi the first burden). That is the playbook's walk-away case, so the clause fails even the fallback.
- **Why preferred, not fallback:** the fallback's 3× annual-fees super-cap would cut back an indemnity that is currently uncapped (Section 14.5 preserves indemnity claims), and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure — we do not weaken our own position to reach a checklist element.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new limbs (d) IP infringement/misappropriation by the RevMed Licensed Technology or our exercise of the licences and (e) unauthorised access to or disclosure of Sanofi Confidential Information/data caused by RevMed, with the "(a) through (c)" cross-reference conformed to "(e)"; and Section 14.2 narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Deterministic failures:
- vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: failed

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred checklist is complete on the operative language: the two inserted limbs (IP infringement/misappropriation and unauthorised access/disclosure of Sanofi data) close the only real gaps, and the retained 14.1(a)/(c) plus the Section 14.3 notice, control-of-defence and cooperation machinery supply the remaining elements.
- The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" is a wording-level false negative: it appears to look for "Services"/"Deliverables" infringement language, which does not exist in this collaborative research/licence agreement. Substantively, new 14.1(d) is a full Vendor IP indemnity covering both the RevMed Licensed Technology and Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences.
- Fallback level is deliberately not taken and is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3x cap). That is acceptable because the preferred level is complete, and the rationale for declining the super-cap (it would introduce a cap on a presently uncapped indemnity and "annual fees" has no analogue in a milestone/royalty structure) is sound.
- Minimality holds: the edits are confined to adding limbs (d) and (e), conforming the "(a) through (e)" cross-reference, and rewriting Section 14.2 to the two permitted limbs. No survival tails, expense allocations, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and favourable retained language (uncapped indemnity via 14.5; the pro-Customer 14.1 carve-out structure) is preserved.
- Verify that "RevMed Licensed Technology" is the exact defined term used in the Agreement (it is not among the resolved definitions supplied). If the defined term is, e.g., "RevMed Technology" or "RevMed Licensed Patents and RevMed Know-How", limb (d) will contain an undefined term and must be conformed.
- Housekeeping on Section 14.2: with (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]", the list punctuation/conjunction should be conformed (limb (a) should not end with "or" running into an omitted tail), and any closing "except in each case ((a) through (d))" flush paragraph or other cross-reference to 14.2(c)-(d) elsewhere in the Agreement or the Ancillary Agreements (Profit/Loss Share, Co-Promotion) should be checked so no dangling reference survives.
- Commercial flag for the negotiator, not a checklist defect: deleting former 14.2(a)/(b) removes Sanofi's indemnity for its own Development/Commercialization activities and its own negligence. That narrowing is exactly what the preferred element requires, but expect strong pushback in a collaboration where Sanofi commercialises the Product; RevMed's 14.1 carve-out (i) for Sanofi negligence still protects RevMed on that axis.
- Optional hardening: because limbs are already being inserted, consider an express "(f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law" limb. Breach of law is currently reached only indirectly through 14.1(c) "material breach ... of its obligations" read with the Section 13.4(b) "in all material respects" compliance covenant, so non-material or non-performance-related legal breaches sit outside the indemnity.
- Cross-check Section 10.7 (obligation to negotiate Third Party licences) and any associated cost allocation against new 14.1(d) so the two do not read as competing allocations of Third Party licence cost; the 14.1 "except ... (iii) any breach by Sanofi of its obligations" tail could otherwise be argued to bite where Sanofi has not pursued a 10.7 licence.
